hook.line: Hotels, flats and companies do not just "have" things in a brochure. They have them in a more polished way, and you will meet these verbs on every listing.
hook.en: The flat has a parking space.

examples.es: Contamos con el apoyo de todo el equipo.
examples.en: We have the support of the whole team.
The flat has a parking space.

examples.es: Todos los estudiantes tienen acceso a la biblioteca.
examples.en: All students have access to the library.

rule:
In formal Spanish, *tener* gets three polished replacements:

*contar con*: *El hotel cuenta con piscina.*
*disponer de*: *El apartamento dispone de parqueadero.* *No dispongo de tiempo.*
*tener acceso a*: *Tienen acceso a la biblioteca.*

Each keeps its small word: *con*, *de*, *a*. *Contar con* here means "have", not "count".

*Disponer* is irregular like *poner*: *dispongo, dispone, disponemos*.

For casual talk, *tener* is still right: *El café tiene wifi.*
smallPrint: Teachers call these formal equivalents of *tener*. *Disponer de* often implies something available for use.

options: The flat has a parking space.
The flat is next to a parking lot.
The hotel is waiting for a pool.

yourTurn.prompt: Choose *de* or *con*: El apartamento dispone ___ parqueadero. Type the whole sentence.
Choose *con* or *de*: El hotel cuenta ___ piscina. Type the whole sentence.

yourTurn.why: *Disponer de* with *no* says you lack something.

yourTurn.prompt: All students have access to the library.
yourTurn.answer: Todos los estudiantes tienen acceso a la biblioteca.

yourTurn.prompt: We have the support of the whole team.
yourTurn.answer: Contamos con el apoyo de todo el equipo.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it *we*: No dispongo de tiempo.
Make it formal, to one person: ¿Tienes tiempo mañana?

pitfalls.why: Almost. *Disponer* always needs *de* before what you have.
Almost. In this sense *contar* needs *con*, otherwise it means "count".

personal: Tell us one thing your home or workplace has, in formal style: *Mi apartamento cuenta con…* or *Dispongo de…*.
